Usage

Count rate [Hz] -> counts counts. An exit of countrate (reversible).

The units are the whole content of the conversion: [1/s] * [s] = [1]. gate_s is the integration window in seconds, default 1 ms. counts is the type "photon count per time bin", so letting a rate series call itself counts passes silently with the magnitude off by 7 orders (TYPE_CHECKS only checks both as "non-negative 1-D").

A round trip with counts_to_countrate measures max|Δ| = 9.3e-10 (the range is 1e3-1e7 Hz, so that is relative 1e-16 = 1 unit of double-precision rounding. Looking only at the absolute value it looks large, so quantities spanning many orders of magnitude, like rates, are stated relatively).

★Applying it 2 times raises no exception. TYPE_TO_SORT folds countrate into counts, so the output connects straight back to the input. Measured (2026-09-08, 1,200 Hz with a 1 ms gate): 1.2000 counts after 1 pass, 0.0012 counts after 1 more pass —— a 1,000-fold mix-up passes without producing a negative value or a NaN. There is no way to judge "rate or count" from the values alone, so this one case can only be guarded not by a check but by the caller's discipline (write down the path you connected).

Args:

countrate: (N,) non-negative rate [Hz].

gate_s: integration window [s]. > 0.

Returns:

(N,) float64 non-negative counts.

Raises:

ValueError: negative rate / gate_s <= 0 / invalid shape / non-finite.

The reprconv op countrate_to_counts bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps gate_s (default 0.001). b is unused.
